title: Mixed-state replica-transfer program synthesis
difficulty_explanation: Each seeded trial contains two independent 64-qubit purifications and 96 total overlapping p2/p3/p4 queries. Dense purifications, density matrices, and explicit fourth replicas are impossible. A valid submission must derive one generic cyclic-permutation compiler, recover the exact unique prefix-trie program, traverse it with depth-first liveness, match continuous moments, and return exact graph, operation, memory, and digest certificates. Across four host seeds the canonical programs require only 23.6% to 29.9% of the local transfers in disjoint per-query paths, so a separately transcribed path program is structurally rejected.
solution_explanation: The expert prepares each purified state as an exact bond-four TensorCircuit MPS, derives einsum labels generically from the requested permutation order and exponent, compiles all query selector strings into one canonical order-separated trie, and evaluates that trie depth first while retaining only the active ancestor path. It returns the moments and a canonical JSON digest of the same graph.
verification_explanation: The evaluator never imports TensorCircuit. It independently evolves a complex128 NumPy MPS, constructs local replica transfers with NumPy's integer-subscript einsum API rather than the expert's string compiler, rebuilds the unique trie, and recomputes both certificates. A separate two-system/two-environment dense canary compares matrix powers of explicitly partial-transposed reduced states, an explicit k-copy permutation of the dense purification, and the generic transfer for k=2,3,4.
relevant_experience: This reserve combines Stinespring purification, exact MPS routing, reduced-state partial-transpose moments, generic permutation-network compilation, multi-query common-subexpression elimination, canonical graph serialization, and liveness-aware memory certification.

contract.determinism_scope: Exact public case bytes are bound by the pinned image/runtime and evaluator-emitted full case_digest; the integer seed alone is not a cross-NumPy case identity.

seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: One NumPy Generator stream emits two ordered 32-system/32-environment cases, each with two complex brickwork layers, local damping, five seeded tail segments, and a shuffled bank of sixteen queries at each of orders two, three, and four.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: Exact public cases are deterministic only under the bound runtime and are identified by the full evaluator-emitted case_digest.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, and allow_nan false over the exact two-case public config before case_digest is added; stdout emits protocol_seed and the full digest in exactly one orbit_q_case_identity JSON record.
seed_protocol.seed_scrub: The evaluator removes ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED and all parsed evaluator CLI arguments immediately after emitting case identity and before constructing the independent oracle or importing the submitted module.
seed_protocol.pinned_numpy_note: The target image pins NumPy 2.2.6. Trial manifests must bind the full case_digest and image/runtime; local host digests are not authorized trial records.

difficulty_levers: each trial has two 64-qubit purifications, so neither dense state nor density-matrix shortcuts are viable
sixteen second-, sixteen third-, and sixteen fourth-order queries per case require one order-generic replica-permutation compiler
forward, reverse, and identity local permutations vary across seeded shared segments without publishing an einsum or index map
the exact canonical prefix trie rejects duplicate per-query contraction paths and compresses transfer count by more than threefold on all checked seeds
a depth-first live-environment certificate forces a bounded-memory schedule rather than retaining every graph node
opaque identities, shuffled query order, continuous moments, graph terminals, exact certificates, and a program digest are all scored
the 160-line expert ceiling makes three separately hard-coded replica networks and redundant query evaluators unattractive
claim_boundary: This is a deterministic synthetic exact-moment and contraction-program diagnostic, not a finite-shot randomized-measurement experiment. Graph validation proves that the returned program is the minimal shared prefix trie, but functional output alone cannot prove that an implementation used that graph to compute moments; source audit and runtime/memory telemetry remain necessary. Local validation does not establish TensorCircuit feasibility or model hardness. No Docker, Harbor, canonical-task, verifier-policy, or solver-model trial has run.

local_static_validation.binding_status: non-binding local design canaries only; no listed digest is authorized for a solver trial

admission_blockers: Candidate 117 intentionally has no entry in the frozen candidates.jsonl/shortlist and now has an exact-byte post-snapshot design_only registry binding. The safe runner rejects that lifecycle before both expert and model paths; only a future separately hashed, human-reviewed executable-promotion contract may authorize a run. Do not append or remap it into the frozen 1,000-contract snapshot.

Run the expert in the pinned TensorCircuit image and verify exact bond-four capping, custom-gate orientation, exposed tensor order, generic eight-replica-index backend.einsum support, graph certificate parity, runtime below the 180-second expert target, and measured peak RSS below the frozen envelope.
Independently verify that no nonzero Schmidt value is discarded by the four-bond cap for every prequalification case; a cap-induced approximation invalidates the exact-moment contract.

Prequalify at least 25 exact pinned-image records with protocol_seed, full case_digest, expert output, program digest, operation ratio, live-memory certificate, bond profile, moment margins, runtime, peak memory, and explicit admission status before any solver schedule.

Complete authenticated expert-only functional, static-policy, and LLM-policy audits, including evidence that the moments were computed by traversing the returned shared program rather than by separate paths followed by a fabricated certificate.

Human reviewers must sign the replica-cycle convention, partial-transpose subsystem, canonical trie ordering, terminal mapping, conservative live-memory charge, exact bond-cap claim, oracle independence, and post-snapshot provenance before promotion.

Treat the candidate as HOLD for hardness until an independent prompt audit judges that deriving a generic permutation compiler plus shared traversal is materially non-recipe-exposed; a pinned expert pass would establish feasibility, not model hardness.
exploitability_risks: The functional evaluator can prove that a returned graph is canonical but cannot prove that submitted moments were produced by executing it. Source audit, runtime comparison, and process telemetry must reject certificate fabrication after independent per-query contractions.
The shared layout segments are public execution inputs. Hardness must come from generic replica semantics and correct shared execution, not from hiding the existence of repeated prefixes.
The shallow exact bond-four MPS is classically tractable. Static policy must reject a standalone NumPy simulator even though such a simulator could fit the mathematical workload.
Published evaluator, expert, and host seeds are contaminated development evidence and cannot establish private model hardness.
numerical_statistical_risks: Fourth-order transfers carry eight virtual indices, so a one-step bond increase changes environment size by a high power and can invalidate runtime or memory admission.
TensorCircuit and the NumPy oracle may make different numerical rank decisions; the explicit bond-four cap and pinned parity records are mandatory.
The graph live-memory certificate excludes backend einsum workspace and Python/TensorCircuit overhead; pinned peak RSS remains a separate admission measurement.
This exact deterministic task has no sampling uncertainty and must not be described as finite-shot robustness evidence.
api_risks: MPSCircuit.apply_adjacent_double_gate with max_singular_values=4 must preserve the exact state rather than truncate a physical Schmidt component.
MPSCircuit.get_tensors may expose arbitrary gauges and center positions; all replica moments must remain gauge invariant.
The TensorCircuit NumPy backend einsum must accept dynamically compiled expressions with one rank-eight environment and eight rank-three MPS tensor operands.
TensorCircuit backend and dtype settings are process global, and complex128 is required for fourth-order cancellation accuracy.
NumPy Generator byte-level cases can drift across versions, so trial records must bind exact case_digest rather than treating the seed as complete identity.
